forwarded_headers_mode.description:
Controls how the proxy handles `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`,
`X-Forwarded-Host`, and `Forwarded` headers. Only these proxy-identity
headers are affected; all other request headers pass through unchanged.

- `Preserve` (default): incoming headers are passed through, then Cruma
  appends its own values (client IP, proto, host).
- `StripIncoming`: headers supplied by the upstream client are removed,
  then Cruma adds a fresh set. Use this when the proxy is Internet-facing
  and you cannot trust what arrived.
- `None`: all such headers are removed — both incoming and Cruma's own —
  so the backend receives none.

items.description:
A single path-prefix → target mapping used by `FrontendDefinition.path_routes`.

Exactly one of `backend_id`, `process_id`, or `kubernetes_target_id` must be set.

backend_id.description: Id of a static backend to forward matching requests to.

kubernetes_target_id.description: Id of a Kubernetes target to forward matching requests to.

path_prefix.description:
Path prefix to match (e.g. `/api/`). Longer (more specific) prefixes
take priority over shorter ones regardless of declaration order.

process_id.description: Id of a hosted process spec to forward matching requests to.

request_limits.description: Optional request/header limits applied to this specific path route.

body_read_timeout_secs.description:
Maximum time, in seconds, the client may go **without sending any request
body bytes** before the request is aborted — an *idle* (not total)
timeout, so legitimate large uploads that keep making progress are never
cut off. Bounds slow-body attacks that send headers promptly then dribble
the body to hold a connection open. Opt-in: when unset, no body-read
timeout is enforced (request bodies may stall indefinitely, matching prior
behavior). A route may only tighten the listener's value.

header_read_timeout_secs.description:
Maximum time, in seconds, allowed for a client to send the complete
request header block. Bounds slow-header (slowloris) attacks that dribble
bytes to hold a connection open indefinitely. When unset, a built-in
default of [`DEFAULT_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS`] applies. A route may only
tighten (never loosen) the listener's value.

max_header_bytes.description: Maximum aggregate header bytes across all parsed request headers.

max_header_name_bytes.description: Maximum bytes allowed for a single header name.

max_header_value_bytes.description: Maximum bytes allowed for a single header value.

max_request_body_bytes.description: Maximum accepted request body size in bytes.

tools.name: upsert_frontend

tools.description: Make a local port reachable through this agent's tunnel. Omit access for a public share, or set its closed password, ip_allowlist, or sign_in access policy. Creates (or updates, if the name or port is already exposed) a backend for host:port (default 127.0.0.1) and a tunnel-only frontend at <name>.<assigned domain>, waits up to 30 s for the tunnel to have its public domain, and returns public_url, local_target, frontend_id and account. The share lasts until unexpose or until the agent stops (over the local socket: until that socket connection closes): no config save writes it to the agent's config file, including later persist=true calls. When this connection has applied a project file, the share is also saved to that file (project_file says whether), except a share with a generated or typed password, which is live and not saved: use a ${env:NAME} or ${file:ABSOLUTE_PATH} password reference to have it saved; a folder outside the project's directory is live and not saved. A previewed project is never written. Withdraw it with unexpose.

password.description:

generated when omitted and returned once in the exposure result.

cidrs.description: CIDR networks allowed to reach the share.

signed-in agent.

Creates (or updates by name) a tunnel-only local-directory frontend at <name>.<assigned domain>, waits up to 30 s for a public domain, and returns public_url, local_target, frontend_id and account. When this connection has applied a project file, a process of that project is saved to the file (project_file says whether); a process with literal env values is live and not saved, so write secrets as ${env:NAME} or ${file:PATH}. binary_watch.description:
Configuration for watching a file or directory for modifications.

When `watch_path` is omitted the supervisor watches the resolved binary
that was used to spawn the process. If `recursive` is enabled, the
default target becomes the process working directory (or the resolved
binary's parent directory when no working directory is configured).

anyOf.description: Log a warning and keep the process running.
Stop and restart the process.

on_change.description: What to do when the path is modified or deleted.

recursive.description:
When `watch_path` is a directory, also watch all subdirectories
recursively.  Has no effect when watching a single file.

watch_path.description:
Path to watch.  Omit to watch the process binary itself, or the
working directory when `recursive` is enabled.
Can be a file or a directory; when a directory, all files directly
inside it are watched (and subdirectories too when `recursive` is true).

env.description:
Environment variables as explicit entries because OpenAI strict tool
schemas cannot represent arbitrary string-to-string maps.

anyOf.description: HTTP/1.1 (default, most compatible).

HTTP/2 — ALPN-negotiated for HTTPS backends; falls back to HTTP/1.1 on
cleartext backends (use `H2PK` for cleartext HTTP/2 via prior knowledge).
HTTP/2 Prior Knowledge — speak HTTP/2 directly without negotiation.

upstream_protocol.description:
HTTP protocol version to use when talking to the upstream backend.

This controls how the proxy speaks to your origin server.  The default
(`H1`) is the safest choice — most local dev servers and backends speak
HTTP/1.1.  Choose `H2` when your backend advertises HTTP/2 via ALPN (HTTPS
backends only); on cleartext (HTTP) backends `H2` sends HTTP/1.1 — use
`H2PK` instead to get cleartext HTTP/2 (prior knowledge).  `H2PK` speaks
HTTP/2 frames directly with no negotiation — useful for gRPC or backends
that *only* speak HTTP/2.

tools.name: upsert_process

tools.description: Send a LIVE route-decision probe: fire a real loopback request through the running proxy on a given listener port and return the decision the actual data plane produced. Unlike `simulate_route` (which reimplements routing offline), this exercises the real accept path and reports which plane handled it (hyper vs io_uring), fast-path eligibility, the classified request/response middleware chains, the TLS decision, and the chosen backend origin (round-robin cursor previewed, not advanced — it never dials the backend). Provide `port` (a bound HTTP-terminating listener; TLS-passthrough and raw-TCP listeners cannot answer), optionally `tls`, `sni`, `host`, `path`, `http2`. Use this to confirm ground truth when `simulate_route`'s prediction is in doubt.

inputSchema.description:
Arguments for `probe_route` — the LIVE counterpart to `simulate_route`. Where `simulate_route`
reimplements routing offline, this fires a real loopback request through the running proxy and
reports the decision the actual data plane produced (including which plane, hyper vs io_uring).

host.description:
HTTP `Host` header. Set it different from `sni` to reproduce the reused-TLS / connection
-coalescing case (a browser reusing a connection for a sibling hostname).

http2.description: Force HTTP/2 (ALPN `h2` over TLS, or prior-knowledge h2c on plaintext). Defaults to HTTP/1.1.

path.description: HTTP request path, e.g. `"/api/v1/foo"`. Defaults to `"/"`. May include a query string.

sni.description: TLS SNI to present at the handshake. Optional; defaults to `host`.

tls.description:
Whether the listener terminates TLS. Optional — if omitted, inferred from the live config's
listener on that port (defaults to plaintext when unknown).

tools.name: probe_route

tools.description: Return the current machine-local firewall rules with live per-rule hit counts, plus the current runtime auto-blocked IPs inserted by WAF auto-ban. Firewall rules filter incoming connections by source IP/CIDR, protocol, port, and hostname/SNI before any HTTP processing.
tools.name: get_firewall_rules

tools.description: Add a new firewall rule or replace an existing one by zero-based index. Omit index to append. Persists immediately to the machine-local settings file and updates the live runtime.

index.description: Zero-based index of the rule to replace. Omit to append a new rule.

anyOf.description:
Drop the connection without responding. Enforced as early as
possible: at connection accept when the rule needs no hostname/SNI,
right after the ClientHello for TLS connections, per request
otherwise.

Respond with an HTTP status code. HTTP traffic only; raw TCP
connections fall back to being dropped.

deny_behavior.description: What to do with denied traffic. Ignored for allow rules.

hostname.description: Hostname / SNI glob (e.g. `"*.example.com"`). Empty string means any.

anyOf.description: Port filter for a firewall rule. `None` on the owning field means any port.

source_cidr.description: Source IP or CIDR (e.g. `"192.168.1.0/24"`). Empty string means any.

tools.name: upsert_firewall_rule

tools.description: Return the current machine-local WAF (Web Application Firewall) rules with live per-rule hit counts. WAF rules inspect HTTP request fields (path, method, user-agent, query string) and can block or drop matching requests.
tools.name: get_waf_rules

tools.description: Add a new WAF rule or replace an existing one by zero-based index. Omit index to append. Persists immediately to the machine-local settings file and updates the live runtime.

index.description: Zero-based index of the rule to replace. Omit to append a new rule.

anyOf.description: Return HTTP 403 Forbidden.
Return HTTP 404 Not Found (reveals less about what's protected).
Drop the connection without a response.

action.description: What to do when a WAF rule matches.

auto_ban.description: How long to auto-ban a matching IP.

match_field.description: Which part of the HTTP request a WAF rule inspects.

pattern.description: Exact match by default; use `*` for wildcard matching.

tools.name: upsert_waf_rule
list_agents
tools.description: List the Cruma agents running for this user (the desktop app, headless agents, and this session's own agent) and the profiles that are not running. Each running agent shows its `version` and release `channel` (stable and preview agents can run side by side), when it started (`started_at`, `age_secs`) and who started it (`starter`: user_start, installed_service, desktop_app or coding_session with the client and process id when known, unknown for an agent that does not record it), plus its tunnel domain, whether the tunnel is anonymous or signed-in account state, its server-reported tunnel plan when known, its sites (hostnames) and hosted processes, whether changes made here are saved, and whether it also serves HTTP /mcp. The build, start and starter facts show even when an agent does not answer in time; the live facts then are absent. `attached` marks the agent every other tool here talks to. A profile that is not running comes with a `start_hint`; this tool never starts one.

tools.name: use_agent
tools.description: Switch this session to one of the running agents from list_agents, by `id` (or by `profile` name). Every tool afterwards talks to that agent, and the ports this session exposed on the previous agent are withdrawn. A project file this window attached stays on the shared session agent: switching to the user's own agent withdraws it, it is not attached to that agent, and switching back to the session agent attaches it again. Ask the user before switching to their own agent. A profile that is not running cannot be chosen: the answer carries the hint for starting it.

id.description: The `id` of a running agent, from list_agents.

profile.description:
The name of a profile whose agent is running, from list_agents. Use
either `id` or `profile`.

tools.name: stop_agent
tools.description: Stop a temporary agent from list_agents by `id` (or `profile`). Only an agent owned by a coding session can be stopped; a kept agent and agents deliberately started by the user, desktop app or installed service return a typed refusal. The target cancels itself through its owner-only local endpoint and shuts down its shares and tunnels normally.

tools.name: open_desktop_app
tools.description: Open the Cruma desktop app on this machine, or bring it forward when it is already running, so the user can see the tunnels and settings set up here. Call it only when the user asks to see them. Never call it in CI or on a machine without a screen. `status` is `opened`, `focused` or `unavailable`; unavailable carries a `reason` (`no_gui_in_this_build`, `no_display`, `not_installed`, `launch_failed`) and an `install_hint`.
